answers.answer: Supported theorem: at fixed global phase twist Θ, the equilibrium free energy is the global minimum over all internal condensate amplitudes and relative phases, F(Θ)=min F[Θ;|Δ|,α]. On one connected superconducting interval (Θ_c^−,Θ_c^+), with conventional local thermodynamics and continuous endpoint matching F(Θ_c^+)=F(Θ_c^−), I(Θ)=2e∂_ΘF and I_c^±=max_Θ[±I(Θ)]. Exact I_c^−=0 with I_c^+≠0 would make I≥0 everywhere and positive somewhere, so ∫I dΘ>0 contradicts endpoint equality. Exact equilibrium perfection is therefore forbidden. The asymptotic limit ε=I_c^−/I_c^+→0 requires a nonanalytic/singular global free-energy landscape: branch switching, competing condensates, or textures/domain walls producing broad nearly-flat negative-current regions and finite positive-current regions. A smooth analytic single branch cannot realize the limit by the identity theorem.

answers.answer: The regularity assumptions are model-class specific. The basic veto requires global minimization at fixed Θ, a connected superconducting domain (with reentrant intervals asserted to extend straightforwardly), and continuity of F at the superconducting endpoints. For a finite-order Landau description, I is assumed to be a real polynomial of degree ≤n, giving ε≥[T_n((1+r)/(1−r))]^{-1}. For a 2π-periodic Josephson energy with harmonics through order n, ε≥[T_{2n}(sec(πr/2))]^{-1}; finite 4π periodicity only changes the fundamental domain. If F∈C^k but F∉C^{k+1}, Fourier tails scale as |A_m|∼m^{−(k+1)} and |I_m|∼m^{−k}, weakening the finite-harmonic obstruction. These quantitative bounds are not universal bounds on unrestricted nonsmooth or infinite-harmonic models.

answers.answer: The theorem concerns unconstrained two-terminal global equilibrium. It explicitly includes multiband/multicomponent condensates, finite-momentum paired states, and effectively one-dimensional Josephson devices only when all internal variables globally relax at fixed Θ. It does not govern constrained equilibrium, selected local-minimum or loss-of-stability dynamics, metastable current-biased Josephson switching, explicitly driven/dissipative states, or multiterminal devices. Those routes can produce high or ideal measured efficiency without contradicting the theorem.

answers.answer: The explicit solvable model is a per-length free energy f=F/L with q=Θ/L and an internal Ising variable σ=±1: f(q;σ)=−f_0+(K_σ/2)q²−σγ_σq, with K_σ>0 and γ_σ>0. Minimizing σ gives f(q<0)=−f_0+(K_−/2)q²+γ_−q and f(q>0)=−f_0+(K_+/2)q²−γ_+q, with a cusp at q=0 (or a shifted cusp measured relative to its location). The superconducting cutoffs are q_c^±=±K_±^{-1}(γ_±+√(γ_±²+2K_±f_0)), and minima q_*^±=±γ_±/K_±. The current is I(q)=2e(K_−q+γ_−) for q_c^−<q<0 and 2e(K_+q−γ_+) for 0<q<q_c^+, with a jump 2e(γ_++γ_−) at q=0. I_c^±=2e max(γ_∓,γ_±+√(γ_±²+2K_±f_0)). The complete toy-model data are (f_0,K_+,K_−,γ_+,γ_−), subject to positivity; near-perfect asymmetry requires γ_−, γ_+, and K_−→0 with K_+=f_0 fixed. The displayed examples are (1,1,0.7,0.8,0.35), ε≈0.759, and (1,1,0.003,0.01,0.01), ε≈5.5×10^−2.

answers.answer: For a helical Lifshitz endpoint, the requirement already supplied by this paper is not merely ‘criticality’ or a local soft mode: near-perfect global-equilibrium diode behavior requires that global minimization generate a nonanalytic lower envelope F(Θ), with branch switching or an equivalent singular texture/order rearrangement. The supplied paper does not analyze a helical Lifshitz endpoint or prove that its local criticality produces such a global singular branch. Therefore the endpoint application remains unresolved and model-specific.

answers.answer: A local finite-wavevector pairing instability is not, by itself, an exception to the theorem and is insufficient evidence for the required branch. If all competing states are globally minimized at fixed Θ and their lower envelope is continuous but nonanalytic, the instability can realize the permitted singular-branch mechanism. A globally competing multi-q order likewise lies inside the theorem only after a complete global free-energy comparison; if the observed state is a selected local/metastable branch, it is outside the theorem and becomes model-specific. The source supplies no microscopic multi-q functional, fluctuation analysis, barrier calculation, or global-versus-local result for such a case.

answers.answer: The unresolved consequential science is therefore not another proof of continuity, the identity theorem, polynomial rigidity, or finite-harmonic bounds. It is the complete model-specific determination of whether a specified material or endpoint has: (i) all microscopic parameters and competing q/multi-q order parameters specified; (ii) a globally minimized, continuous but singular F(Θ); (iii) equilibrium access across competing branches rather than metastability; and (iv) a measurement protocol sampling that global state. The supplied source does not provide those data or calculations.
